Call Transcript -- Case #55231 (transcribed)

Agent: Thank you for calling NimbusNet support, this is Callie, how can I help you today?
Customer: Hi Callie, before anything else, do you need to verify my account?
Agent: Yes please, can I get your name and the last four digits of the account number?
Customer: Sure, it's Owen Bennett, account ending 4471.
Agent: Great, thank you Owen, I have your account pulled up now. What can I help with?
Customer: A couple things actually. First, just a quick one -- the replacement router you sent me back in March, is that fully paid off now?
Agent: Let me check... yes, that was a one-time $0 replacement under warranty, no balance attached to it at all. That account line shows closed and paid in full as of March.
Customer: Good, glad that's settled. The bigger issue is my bill. I've been a customer for 6 years and I'm frustrated. My bill jumped from $79.99 to $134.99 this month and nobody told me why.
Agent: I'm sorry about that, let me pull up your billing history... I see a promotional rate expired last cycle. Your last three bills were: June $79.99, July $79.99, and August $134.99. The standard rate for your plan is $134.99.
Customer: I was never told the promo would end. I want it extended, or at least a $55 credit to cover the difference this month.
Agent: I understand the frustration. Let me check what I can offer... I can't authorize a full $55 credit on my own, that's above my threshold. Let me put you on hold to check with my supervisor.
[Hold - 4 minutes]
Agent: Thanks for your patience, Owen. My supervisor authorized a one-time $30 credit as a goodwill gesture, but couldn't approve extending the promotional rate itself -- that program has fully ended for all customers.
Customer: $30 is less than what I asked for, but okay, I'll take it. Can you also confirm my new baseline rate going forward is $134.99, not something else?
Agent: Confirmed, $134.99 per month starting next cycle, plus the one-time $30 credit applied to this month's bill.
Customer: Alright. One more thing -- my neighbor said she got her promo extended for another 6 months when she called last week. Why can't I get that?
Agent: I can't speak to another customer's account specifics, but as I mentioned, that promotional program closed company-wide as of the end of last month, so no new extensions are being granted regardless of when someone calls.
Customer: Okay, I guess I'll take the $30 then. Thanks for checking. It's frustrating because I never got an email or text saying the promo was ending -- if I'd known, I would have called before the bill even changed.
Agent: That's fair feedback, and I'll note it on the account. Going forward, promo-expiration notices are supposed to go out 14 days before the change, but I can see there was a system issue last cycle that affected a batch of these notices, yours included.
Agent: You're welcome. Is there anything else I can help with today?
Customer: No, that's it. Actually, can you email me a confirmation of all this -- the credit, the new rate, and the reason the promo ended?
Agent: Absolutely, I'll send that to the email on file within the hour. It'll include today's case number, 55231, for your records.
Customer: Perfect, thank you.
Agent: Great, you should see the $30 credit reflected within 1-2 billing cycles. Have a great day, Owen.

Call Summary (auto-generated): Customer requested a $55 goodwill credit and/or promo extension. Resolution: $30 one-time credit approved by supervisor; promo extension denied (program ended company-wide). New baseline rate confirmed at $134.99/month. No further action items.
